title: PCR Amplification of Gibson Assembly Fragments for the BM3R1/PhlF Genetic Circuit
author: Varsha Athreya
materials: Cap tubes, flick to mix, and pulse-spin.
If your thermocycler does not have a heated lid, overlay each reaction with ~25 µL mineral oil to prevent evaporation during cycling. Skip this step on any modern heated-lid instrument.

Verify amplification by gel electrophoresis Cast a 1% agarose gel in 1X TAE with SYBR Safe (or equivalent stain). Load 5 µL of each PCR reaction alongside 5 µL of Quick-Load Purple 1 kb Plus DNA Ladder (NEB N0550S). Run at 100 V for ~30 min (until the dye front has migrated ~⅔ down the gel). Image the gel on a UV or blue-light transilluminator. Confirm a single band at the expected size for each fragment, and that all NTC lanes are empty.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Master Mix
steps.instruction: Assemble the PCR components in the specified order: water, buffer, dNTPs, primers, template, and polymerase.

substeps.instruction: Mix gently by flicking (do not vortex after adding enzyme).
Briefly spin to collect liquid at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Aliquot Master Mix and Add Primers
steps.instruction: Distribute the master mix into labeled PCR tubes and add the specific primers.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the master mix into each labeled PCR tube.
Add 2.5 µL of the appropriate 10 µM forward primer and 2.5 µL of the corresponding 10 µM reverse primer (final concentration 0.5 µM each).

steps.title: Add Template DNA
steps.instruction: Add the plasmid template or water for controls to the PCR tubes.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL of plasmid template (1 pg–1 ng total).
For No Template Controls (NTCs), substitute 1 µL nuclease-free water for the template.

steps.title: Purify and Quantify Amplicons
steps.instruction: Clean up the PCR products and determine their concentration.

substeps.instruction: Purify each PCR product using the Monarch Spin PCR DNA Cleanup Kit (NEB T1130) according to manufacturer instructions.
Elute in 20 µL nuclease-free water or elution buffer.
Quantify each cleaned amplicon using Qubit dsDNA HS or NanoDrop.
Record the concentration (ng/µL) and A260/A280 in the run record.
Use fragments within 1 week for optimal assembly efficiency.

description: Each PCR reaction yields a single, sharp band on the gel at the expected size for that fragment. All NTC lanes are clean (no bands). Post-cleanup yield: typically 10–50 ng/µL in 20 µL elution (200 ng–1 µg total per fragment), sufficient for multiple Gibson Assembly reactions. A260/A280 ratios between 1.8 and 2.0 indicate clean, protein-free DNA suitable for downstream assembly. No band: Re-check primer Tm calculation; lower the annealing temperature by 2–3 °C; verify template concentration (1 pg–1 ng plasmid); add 1X Q5 High GC Enhancer for GC-rich amplicons (e.g., Pxyl-tetO region). Multiple bands / smearing: Raise annealing temperature by 2–3 °C; reduce template by 10×; redesign primers to improve specificity; reduce cycle number to 25. Band in NTC lane: Discard primer aliquots and remake from frozen stock; use filter tips; UV-decontaminate the PCR setup area. Failed Gibson downstream: Re-run amplicons on a gel after cleanup to confirm no carryover primer-dimer; ensure ≥20 bp Gibson overlaps in primer design; balance fragment molar ratios in the assembly reaction.
